analyst_view.overall: Early view: Bodo/Glimt sit 25th with 4 points after a 0-0 at home to Lille on matchday 4, while LASK climbed to 16th by beating bottom side Slovan Bratislava 4-0. I found little fresh team news for either club, so this view rests mainly on the matchday 4 results and the table; a late-November night on the artificial pitch at Aspmyra is the one thing the numbers may underrate.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, which looks high for this pairing. Bodo/Glimt's last home game in this competition was a 0-0 with Lille, and LASK's 4-0 came against a Slovan side that has lost every game, so I would not read too much into it. I expect something nearer three goals than four.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners and I have nothing that moves it. Bodo/Glimt kept pressing at home against Lille without scoring, which usually means corners, but LASK's win over Slovan came mostly from open play and a free kick. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and I lean slightly lower. The Bodo/Glimt v Lille game produced only two bookings, and LASK's win over Slovan had two, both for the visitors. Neither side has shown a pattern of feisty European games so far.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots. Bodo/Glimt kept attacking in the goalless draw with Lille, and LASK showed against Slovan that they will shoot from set plays and distance (Kasper Jorgensen scored a free kick). Nothing I found points away from the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, which needs both sides to be sharp. Bodo/Glimt failed to score at home to Lille, and LASK's finishing against Slovan came against the weakest defence in the competition. I expect a little fewer efforts on target than the estimate.

note: No estimate: Champions League teams come from different leagues, and their numbers can't be compared reliably yet. Full stats appear here after the match.
